top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: A collapsing glacier sent a wall of ice, mud and rock down a Himalayan river on Wednesday, and by Thursday evening Nepali police put the death toll at 359, with more than 1,000 people still missing across Nepal and Tibet. The other running story is Washington's: the Justice Department says a Chinese state-sponsored group broke into NASA, the Federal Reserve and the Senate, which Beijing calls smearing, while Canada's dollar-for-dollar tariffs on US goods take effect on Sept 8. Elsewhere the day ran to loss and litigation, from wildfires that killed at least 12 in Algeria to an $18 billion Meta settlement that Brussels now wants matched in Europe. If you follow one thing tomorrow, make it the Nepal search - the great majority of the missing are still unaccounted for, and the toll has moved every few hours.

stories.headline: Glacier collapse triggers Himalayan flash flood; at least 362 dead, more than 1,000 missing
stories.summary: A wall of ice, mud and rock collapsed into a mountain river on Wednesday, sending a catastrophic flash flood down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli valleys along the Nepal-Tibet border. Nepali police put the death toll at 359 as of 5pm local time on Thursday; Chinese state media reported three more deaths at the Gyirong border hub, taking the total to at least 362. More than 1,000 people are missing across the two countries, including 558 in Tibet's Gyirong county according to state broadcaster CCTV, and over 650 foreigners in Nepal. Scientists say a collapsing glacier is the likely trigger. China's Premier Li Qiang visited the Gyirong site on Thursday afternoon.

stories.headline: US disrupts Chinese state hacking platforms; Beijing calls the allegations 'smearing'
stories.summary: The US Justice Department and FBI said they had seized internet domains used by a Chinese state-sponsored group known as QTFY and by two hacking platforms, QScan and QTRouter. US officials said victims of the intrusions included NASA, the Federal Reserve, the US Senate and the departments of justice, energy, and health and human services. China's foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian on Thursday called the allegations 'false information' and accused Washington of 'distorting right and wrong' under the pretext of cybersecurity.
stories.source: CNA (US Justice Department, Chinese foreign ministry)

stories.headline: Canada drops seafood from its retaliatory tariff list as trade war with US widens
stories.summary: Canada's finance department said it had removed seafood and fish products from its list of counter-tariffs on US imports, a day after announcing levies on about US$20 billion of American goods. Ottawa is matching Washington dollar for dollar after the US imposed new 50 per cent tariffs on Canadian imports on Saturday. The Canadian measures take effect on Sept 8. President Donald Trump said it was 'time to teach Canada you can't do this anymore'.
stories.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Canada Department of Finance)

stories.headline: EU tells Meta to match its US teen-safety settlement in Europe
stories.summary: A day after Meta agreed to an approximately US$18 billion settlement with US state attorneys general over claims Facebook and Instagram were designed to encourage compulsive use by teenagers, the European Commission said it expects the company to address 'addictive' features in Europe too. The Commission found Meta in breach of the Digital Services Act last month. 'The ball is in Meta's court,' spokesman Thomas Regnier said, adding that Brussels is probing Meta over 'exactly the same suspicions' raised in the US case. The settlement still needs court approval.

stories.headline: Pentagon presses NATO allies to show how they will take over Europe's defence
stories.summary: US Defense Under Secretary Elbridge Colby, visiting NATO headquarters in Brussels, asked European allies to explain how they are meeting Washington's demands to take primary responsibility for their own conventional defence. The Trump administration launched a six-month review of US deployments in Europe in July, raising fears among allies of troop cuts, and has sent European capitals a questionnaire on their progress. Separately, US officials said the Pentagon's posture review is preparing troop-level options for Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth by Nov 6.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times (US Defense Department)

stories.headline: Qatar's prime minister visits Tehran to pursue mediation
stories.summary: Qatar's prime minister travelled to Tehran on Thursday to pursue mediation efforts, opening a second Gulf channel alongside Oman's talks with Iran on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The visit comes six months into the war that began on Feb 28, and days after Washington announced a new sanctions package on Aug 24 aimed at Iran's oil revenues, banks and trading partners.

stories.headline: Norway's King Harald V in 'extremely serious' condition as royal family gathers
stories.summary: Norway's royal household said King Harald V, 89, is in an 'extremely serious' condition at Oslo University Hospital, where he has been treated for over a week for a rare blood condition, haemolytic anaemia. Queen Sonja and Crown Prince Haakon have cancelled all royal engagements and gathered at his bedside with other family members. Harald has been on the throne since 1991 and is Europe's oldest head of state.
stories.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Norwegian royal court)

stories.headline: Two killed as car is driven into a crowd outside Caen station in northern France
stories.summary: Two people were killed and 10 injured when a car was driven into a group of people opposite the train station in Caen, Normandy, French reports say. 'A car deliberately rammed into pedestrians opposite the station,' local prefect David Clavière told reporters, adding that seven of the injured were in a critical condition. A man was arrested after a major emergency response. Witnesses said a fight had broken out between two groups beforehand; the mayor said investigators were still trying to establish the driver's motive. Earlier reports from CNA and The Straits Times gave a toll of one dead.

stories.headline: At least 12 dead as wildfires sweep northern Algeria during severe heatwave
stories.summary: At least 12 people have been killed and dozens injured as dozens of blazes swept through several provinces along Algeria's northern coastline, civil protection authorities said. Interior Minister Said Sayoud said at least 54 people had suffered burn injuries, six of them being treated in intensive care. The fires come as northern Africa endures a severe heatwave affecting Algeria and Tunisia in particular.

stories.headline: FDA approves pancreatic cancer pill that nearly doubled survival in trials
stories.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved daraxonrasib, sold as Rasonque and made by Revolution Medicines, for pancreatic cancer. In a late-stage trial of 500 patients, those on the daily pill survived an average of 13.2 months against 6.6 months on chemotherapy. The drug works by shutting off the mutated KRAS gene found in more than 90 per cent of pancreatic tumours. The FDA called it a 'critical new option' for a historically hard-to-treat cancer.

stories.headline: Nvidia's blowout quarter lifts Asian chip stocks, but sticky US inflation caps the rally
stories.summary: Technology stocks rose on Thursday after Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, reported second-quarter revenues that more than doubled year on year and forecast another strong quarter, easing worries about the AI investment boom. Nvidia shares climbed more than 6 per cent in pre-market trade. Asian markets were mixed and European stocks mostly lower, with US data showing inflation still stubbornly high.

stories.headline: Thousands protest outside Indonesia's parliament demanding stronger anti-corruption measures
stories.summary: Thousands of demonstrators from Jakarta and other parts of Indonesia gathered outside the parliament complex in Senayan on Thursday afternoon, demanding stronger anti-corruption measures alongside wider political and social reforms. About 1,000 came from the GERAM alliance of student and civil society groups. More than 18,000 security personnel were reportedly deployed across the capital.

stories.headline: Former Malaysian PM Ismail Sabri charged over undeclared assets including gold bars
stories.summary: Ismail Sabri Yaakob, 66, pleaded not guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to a charge under Section 36(2) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act. He is accused of failing to declare holdings of nearly US$40 million in ringgit and nine foreign currencies, five Suisse Fine gold bars, a silver bar and a gold coin at MACC headquarters in Putrajaya on Feb 7 last year. He was one of three former Malaysian prime ministers at the court complex the same day, each facing separate legal proceedings.
stories.source: CNA (Bernama, The Edge, Free Malaysia Today)

stories.headline: Yayoi Kusama, the Japanese artist who turned hallucinations into art, dies at 97
stories.summary: Yayoi Kusama, whose polka dots, mirrored infinity rooms and pumpkin sculptures made her one of the world's most recognisable living artists, has died aged 97. She drew on the hallucinations she experienced from childhood, and had lived voluntarily in a Tokyo psychiatric institution since 1977 while working from a studio nearby.

stories.headline: CIA director warned Russia not to attack NATO members during Moscow trip, US media report
stories.summary: US outlets including The Wall Street Journal and CBS News reported that CIA director John Ratcliffe used his unannounced Moscow visit to warn Russia against attacking NATO members. Russia's foreign intelligence chief has confirmed he held talks with Ratcliffe. President Donald Trump has described the trip as a 'semi-routine' mission. Neither government has said what was discussed.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times (WSJ, CBS News, Russian SVR)

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Nine Singaporeans are among the hundreds reported missing after the Nepal-Tibet floods, and MFA has told others in Nepal to stay clear of the affected districts. The response moved quickly - PM Lawrence Wong sent condolences and is assembling a humanitarian package, and the Singapore Red Cross pledged S$50,000 ahead of a public appeal that opens on Friday. Two things to diarise closer to home: the Bukit Panjang LRT shuts all day on Sept 20 and 27 for the last stage of its renewal, and a failed concrete transfer slab at the 63-storey Promenade Peak is being torn out and rebuilt. The courts had another heavy day, with sentences running from a swimming coach jailed for molesting a 10-year-old to eight and a half years for a restaurant chef. The lighter talk is concert-shaped, led by Post Malone's National Stadium show being postponed - worth checking your inbox if you hold tickets, since refunds can take up to 60 business days.

stories.headline: Nine Singaporeans among the missing in Nepal floods; MFA urges caution
stories.summary: The Nepal Tourism Board said nine Singaporeans were among those missing in Rasuwa district as of noon on Thursday, following the flash flood that swept the Nepal-Tibet border a day earlier. Two of them were part of a 47-person tour group that also included Australians, Canadians, Nepalese, Americans and Britons, according to AFP. Rasuwa was hit first, but deaths were reported across seven districts as floodwaters surged more than 160km south to Chitwan. MFA has advised Singaporeans in Nepal to exercise caution and avoid flood-affected areas.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Nepal Tourism Board, MFA)

stories.headline: PM Wong sends condolences over Nepal-China floods; humanitarian package being put together
stories.summary: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong extended condolences to those affected by the Nepal-Tibet flash floods, and MFA said Singapore is putting together a humanitarian assistance package. MFA added that it is in contact with local authorities in both Nepal and China over consular assistance for affected Singaporeans.

stories.headline: Singapore Red Cross pledges S$50,000 for Nepal, public appeal opens Friday
stories.summary: The Singapore Red Cross has pledged S$50,000 (US$39,000) towards relief in flood-hit Nepal, funding drinking water and emergency supplies including tarpaulins, blankets, sleeping mats, first aid kits and body bags. A public fundraising appeal opens on Friday and runs until Nov 30. The organisation has also activated its Restoring Family Links service to help Singapore residents reconnect with loved ones in Nepal and Tibet.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Singapore Red Cross)

stories.headline: SM Lee: Singapore must stay open and keep remaking its economy as the US role shifts
stories.summary: Speaking at Nazarbayev University in Kazakhstan on his first visit to Central Asia, Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong said Singapore must remain open, outward-looking and committed to multilateralism as the United States redefines its role in global security and trade. 'Trade dependencies are being weaponised. Multilateralism is breaking down,' he said, arguing that Washington now puts national security and resilience ahead of economic well-being. He was conferred an honorary professorship by the university.

stories.headline: Bukit Panjang LRT to shut for two full days in September for final renewal works
stories.summary: LTA said in a Facebook post on Aug 27 that train service on the Bukit Panjang LRT will be suspended all day on Sept 20 and Sept 27 for the final stage of its renewal programme, which is due to be completed by the end of 2026. The closures cover engineering works on a new power supply system, MRT-style signalling and a modernised operations control centre. Recent disruptions on the 27-year-old line were traced to faults in the new Power Scada system.

stories.headline: Concrete transfer slab at 63-storey Promenade Peak to be torn out and replaced
stories.summary: A concrete transfer slab at Promenade Peak, a 63-storey condominium under construction in River Valley, failed internal quality checks and is being dismantled and replaced, The Straits Times reported. Allgreen Properties managing director Tho Leong Chye told buyers in a May construction update that joint assessments with main contractor Woh Hup found the slab 'did not meet stringent quality standards', and that full replacement was the 'most prudent and responsible' option. Transfer slabs redistribute load from upper floors to columns or walls below.

stories.headline: En bloc reforms may spark more deals, but analysts do not expect a repeat of 2018
stories.summary: Property analysts told The Straits Times that recent reforms to Singapore's collective sale rules are likely to unlock more en bloc deals, but not a boom on the scale of the 2018 cycle. Higher land and construction costs, tighter financing and cautious developer appetite are expected to keep volumes well below that peak.

stories.headline: Two Malaysians arrested over scheme that compromised Singpass accounts for scam e-wallets
stories.summary: Police said two Malaysian men aged 25 and 47 were arrested on Aug 25 over a coordinated scheme that compromised the Singpass accounts of Singapore citizens and work permit holders. Since early March, at least 20 people have been investigated over LiquidPay accounts registered in their names that received S$110,063 linked to scams; preliminary investigations suggest some may not have known the accounts were created. The operation was run by the police Cyber Command with GovTech's Singpass Trust and Safety team.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Singapore Police Force)

stories.headline: Go-Ahead bus driver assaulted on the job, second such case in three months
stories.summary: Public bus operator Go-Ahead said in a Facebook post on Aug 27 that one of its drivers was assaulted on Aug 16 at about 5.20pm while operating service 2, which runs between Changi Village and Kampong Bahru terminals. The trip was disrupted and the driver was treated at Changi General Hospital before returning to work. A police report has been lodged. It is the second assault on a Go-Ahead driver in three months.

stories.headline: Former swimming coach jailed two years and caned for molesting a 10-year-old student
stories.summary: Quek Yeong Kang, also known as Alex, was sentenced to two years' jail and three strokes of the cane for molesting a 10-year-old student three times in a month. He had claimed trial, alleging the victim fabricated the accusations so she could change coaches. In a judgment released on Thursday, Deputy Principal District Judge Luke Tan convicted him on all three charges, rejecting that account. Four other students gave statements to police, three describing how he tickled students during lessons.

stories.headline: Restaurant chef jailed 8.5 years for sexually assaulting an 11-year-old girl
stories.summary: A Singaporean chef, then 62, was sentenced to eight and a half years' jail for sexually assaulting an 11-year-old girl inside a restaurant while other staff and customers were present. He cannot be caned because he is above 50 years old.

stories.headline: Man who pushed 78-year-old to the ground while defending his father gets nine months' jail
stories.summary: A man who pushed a 78-year-old man to the ground during an altercation, while stepping in to defend his own father, has been sentenced to nine months' jail. The older man died from his injuries.

stories.headline: Ex-Credit Suisse vice-president who forged bank letters has jail term cut on appeal
stories.summary: A former Credit Suisse vice-president, Soh Yuanyi, who forged bank letters in a multimillion-dollar case, had her jail sentence reduced on appeal.

stories.headline: Filipino woman in Cambodia-based scam syndicate targeting Singaporeans jailed 25 months
stories.summary: A 35-year-old Filipino woman who worked for a Cambodia-based scam syndicate targeting victims in Singapore was sentenced to 25 months' jail. She was instructed to speak with a Singaporean English accent when calling victims.

stories.headline: Doctor accused of severing wrong arteries barred from surgery for 18 months
stories.summary: A 54-year-old Singaporean doctor accused of severing the wrong arteries during an operation, causing a patient's death, has been restricted from performing surgery for 18 months. The patient's organs suffered tissue death from inadequate blood supply and she died days after the procedure.

stories.headline: Singapore to explore closer South-east Asia-Central Asia links when it chairs ASEAN in 2027
stories.summary: Singapore will look at how South-east Asia and Central Asia can work more closely together when it takes the ASEAN chair in 2027, The Straits Times reported during Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong's visit to the region.

stories.headline: Youth in Singapore can now turn to trained listeners under a new initiative
stories.summary: A new initiative gives young people in Singapore access to trained volunteer listeners for informal emotional support, aimed at those who want someone to talk to without entering formal counselling.

stories.headline: Singapore retailers retrain staff as livestream and social commerce reshape retail jobs
stories.summary: Retailers in Singapore are retraining shop staff for livestream selling and social-commerce roles as more sales shift onto platforms like TikTok and Instagram, changing what frontline retail work involves.

stories.headline: Post Malone's Singapore concert postponed; ticketholders to get full refunds
stories.summary: Ticketmaster Singapore confirmed on Thursday that Post Malone's Sep 25 show at the National Stadium, part of his Big A** World Tour, has been postponed. The confirmation follows the listing being marked 'Currently Unavailable' days earlier. Citing the organiser, Ticketmaster said buyers will receive full refunds to their original payment method, which may take up to 60 business days to process.

stories.headline: Bruno Mars to play four nights in Singapore in April 2027
stories.summary: The Grammy-winning singer will perform in Singapore for four nights in April 2027 as part of his Romantic tour.

stories.headline: Celebrity DJ Anyma to play his first Singapore show in October
stories.summary: Italian-Egyptian electronic artist Anyma will perform his first-ever Singapore show at Marquee in October.

stories.headline: Huang Yiliang returns to acting after 19 years: like 'a fish back in water'
stories.summary: Former Mediacorp actor Huang Yiliang has returned to acting after a 19-year absence, telling CNA the experience felt like being 'a fish back in water'.

stories.headline: Wild snake caught outside the reptile enclosure at Singapore Zoo
stories.summary: Mandai staff caught a non-venomous wild snake found outside the reptile enclosure at the Singapore Zoo. It was later released back into the wild.

stories.headline: Helper who stole S$677 from her employer sent it to a boyfriend who never showed up
stories.summary: A domestic helper who stole S$677 from her Singapore employer transferred the money to her boyfriend, who then left her waiting at the airport for days. She was arrested at HarbourFront Centre while trying to board a ferry to Batam.

stories.headline: Couple fined after their four dogs escaped and injured a dog being walked by a helper
stories.summary: A couple were fined after their four dogs, including Rottweilers and Cane Corsos, escaped their home and charged at a dog being walked by a domestic helper, injuring it.

stories.headline: LA restaurant Chi Spacca is opening in Singapore with woodfire meats and its famous focaccia
stories.summary: Nancy Silverton's Los Angeles restaurant Chi Spacca, known for its woodfired meats and focaccia, is coming to Singapore.

stories.headline: Plan to turn the Singapore Recreation Club's billiards room into a co-working space heads to trial
stories.summary: A dispute over plans to convert the billiards room at the Singapore Recreation Club into a co-working space is going to a court trial.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Russia fired two Oniks cruise missiles, 258 drones and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles at Ukraine overnight, hitting ports, grain storage and energy sites; Ukraine's air force says it downed nearly 90 per cent of the drones but only seven of the ballistic missiles, and that gap is exactly what Kyiv points at when it asks for more Patriots. Around it the diplomacy got louder than the fighting - Russia's foreign intelligence chief confirmed he met the CIA director in Moscow, and Zelensky's top aide floated Ukraine-Russia talks in September. Moscow, meanwhile, warned it could strike British military targets over Kyiv's use of UK-supplied missiles. In the Gulf the Iran war has passed six months and settled into an economic siege rather than a shooting one, with Qatar's prime minister now flying to Tehran to try mediation alongside Oman. Israel-Gaza and Lebanon were quiet by comparison, with nothing militarily significant in the last 24 hours - which makes the September talks question the one worth watching.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: Air war first, diplomacy second. Russia hit Kyiv and other cities overnight with two Oniks cruise missiles, 258 drones and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles, striking ports, grain storage, energy and industry; Ukraine's air force says it downed nearly 90 per cent of the drones but only seven of the ballistic missiles, the gap Kyiv keeps citing when it asks for Patriots. Alongside that, Russia's foreign intelligence chief has confirmed he met CIA director John Ratcliffe in Moscow, and Zelensky's top aide says Ukraine-Russia talks may be possible in September. Moscow has separately warned it could strike British military targets over Kyiv's use of UK-supplied missiles, and Washington's force-posture review continues to unsettle NATO allies.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.
Major Russian grain export terminals are hit in a Ukrainian attack on a Black Sea port, extending the campaign against Russian export infrastructure.
Russia dismisses the idea of a Black Sea ceasefire, saying it sees no grounds for 'half-measures' that would give the other side a respite.
NATO jets shoot down a drone that entered Latvian airspace, the latest spillover of the air war into alliance territory.
Russia's defence ministry says its summer campaign has resulted in the capture of 19 settlements in southeastern Ukraine. Kyiv has not confirmed the claim.
Ukraine's General Staff says long-range strikes hit the Progress Rocket Space Centre in Samara, some 900km inside Russia, and a military airfield.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv, which struck blocks of flats and warehouses and damaged a children's hospital and a school. CNA's earlier count was 16. The figures are Ukrainian and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Ukraine State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko tells the BBC that critical infrastructure was 'purposefully attacked' for the first time in several months, disrupting hot water supply in parts of the city.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives.

A senior Russian diplomat says Moscow is ready to consider new ideas on a Ukraine peace settlement but only on its own conditions, repeating that any talks must recognise the 'new realities on the ground'.
Russia holds a rare missile test near the disputed islands north of Japan that Tokyo calls the Northern Territories.

Australia charges a 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen with foreign interference, alleging he joined Ukraine's armed forces to gather information on their military activities for Russia. The allegations have not been tested in court.

Russia's FSB says nine people have been arrested for planned attacks and espionage on behalf of Ukraine, according to Russian state agencies. Kyiv has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.
A Ukrainian man wanted over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage is detained in Croatia, the second arrest in the German-led investigation.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, plans a trip to the United States to raise funding for his projects, The Straits Times reports - a sign his domestic challenge to Zelensky has shifted abroad after the wartime-election protests ended.

The BBC's Steve Rosenberg reports petrol shortages spreading in Russia as the cumulative effect of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure reaches ordinary consumers, though he finds little erosion of public support for the war.
Japan lodges a formal protest over Russia's missile test near the disputed Kuril Islands, held days ahead of an expected Putin visit.

Russian drones strike a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's home city, with a second drone hitting about half an hour after the first. Regional military head Oleksandr Hanzha says 16 people were killed and 130 injured, among them 23 children. Zelensky calls the two-wave attack 'cynical and despicable' and says the second strike targeted emergency workers at the scene; the BBC says it verified footage of the second drone hitting the already burning mall. Russia's military has not commented on the mall.
A separate Russian drone strike in the southern Mykolaiv region kills at least four people, three of them children, and wounds a woman, Ukrainian state media report.
The leaders of France, Britain and Germany announce they will co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday.

Russian state agencies report that nine people have been arrested on suspicion of planning attacks and conducting espionage on Ukraine's behalf. The claim comes from Russian authorities and has not been independently verified.
Russia designates the independent news outlet Mediazona a 'foreign agent'.

German authorities are investigating possible Russian links to a weapons cache discovered in woodland, according to reports cited by the BBC. The investigation is unconfirmed by German officials on the record.

Rescuers work through the night in the wreckage of the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre; Hanzha says the death toll reached 16 after another body was recovered overnight, with nine people reported still missing and 29 in a serious condition. Local officials say at least two more people were killed in further Russian strikes early on Saturday. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted transport infrastructure and warehouses.

Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia kill at least 10 people according to Russian regional officials and halt work at a warehouse of the online retailer Ozon in the Samara region. Russia's figures are not independently verified.

The death toll from Friday's double-tap drone strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih rises to 16, with 130 injured and four people still missing, says Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue work may run for two more days.
President Vladimir Putin says Ukraine has opened a 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia will hit back at Ukraine's 'most sensitive economic sectors'.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, visiting Ukraine, condemns what he calls Russia's escalating attacks on civilian areas.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says French President Emmanuel Macron agreed to accelerate deliveries of French air-defence equipment, after Kyiv said a shortage of interceptors was costing lives. Paris has not published a delivery schedule.

Norway's government says it will give Ukraine another 85 billion Norwegian crowns (about US$9.2 billion) in financial support in the 2027 fiscal year, matching its 2026 contribution and split between military and humanitarian spending. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere announced it while visiting Kyiv with Nordic and Baltic leaders.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine believes Russia plans to draft an additional 300,000 troops after Russian parliamentary elections in mid-September, working towards 500,000 overall by 2027, and that Moscow is raising missile production to about 1,300 a year. These are Ukrainian assessments and have not been independently verified; the Kremlin has not confirmed them.

Zelensky rejects holding a wartime election, saying a vote during this kind of war would 'destroy' the country by splitting Ukrainians. It is his first response to ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a poll. Elections in war are prohibited by Ukrainian law and the country has been under martial law since 2022.

Sacked defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov tells the BBC that Zelensky should be asked what he knew about corruption in his government, following a money-laundering investigation announced last week, while saying he never saw the president act corruptly and never received an improper instruction from him. He repeats his call for a wartime vote.

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store says Norway will give Ukraine US$9 billion (about S$11.4 billion) in 2027, matching this year's record level, with most of it going to the military. Baltic and Nordic leaders gather in Kyiv for a summit with President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Zelensky says Ukraine's army faces a US$27 billion deficit and urges the European Union to advance payments on part of a 90 billion euro loan, warning that without about US$10 billion by the end of the year his soldiers will not have enough weapons. He did not give a detailed breakdown.

Ozon reports a fire at its logistics hub in Russia's central Orenburg region after a drone attack and suspends warehouse operations, a day after an Ozon centre in the neighbouring Samara region was hit and an unspecified number of workers wounded.
A Russian attack on the outskirts of the north-eastern city of Kharkiv kills three people, the regional governor says on Telegram.

Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev says drone debris hit a private childcare centre overnight, killing two children and injuring nine people including seven children, and that debris fell on apartment buildings. The Russian account is not independently verified.

Ozon says a 'major fire' is burning at one of its logistics centres in the Krasnodar region after a drone attack, the second consecutive day one of its hubs has been hit. The company says staff were evacuated and there are preliminarily no casualties. Ukraine's defence ministry said on 22 Aug it was extending to Ozon a campaign that has already struck the 15 largest Wildberries logistics hubs.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ozon, Ukrainian defence ministry)

timeline.event: A drone attack on an industrial area in Nevinnomysk, a chemical production centre in the Stavropol region, is repelled, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov says on Telegram.
Zelensky says Ukraine was not behind the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline blasts and that Kyiv is cooperating with the German-led investigation, after two arrests in the case.

Kyiv hosts a meeting of the French- and British-led Coalition of the Willing to discuss stepping up support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia ahead of winter, as Ukraine marks 35 years of independence.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is due to urge US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to take a more active role on Ukraine, The Straits Times reports.
President Volodymyr Zelensky marks 35 years of Ukrainian independence, saying Ukraine wants peace but will not give in to Russian terms.
BBC reports that President Vladimir Putin said on Saturday Ukraine had opened 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia would hit back at Kyiv's most sensitive economic sectors.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says measures are being taken to minimise the impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russia's grain exports, telling reporters that 'all grain intended for export' will be shipped on time and in full. Tit-for-tat attacks on ports and vessels have shuttered grain terminals and forced dozens of cargoes to be delayed or cancelled in peak export season.

Zelensky says Russia is 'not ready' for a ceasefire limited to attacks on Black Sea ships carrying agricultural produce, because Moscow wants any deal extended to cover strikes on Russian refineries and pipelines.

Ukrainian drone strikes set fire to logistics centres belonging to Ozon, Russia's second-largest online retailer, in Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol and Adygea. The BBC verified video of the attacks. Ozon said several people were injured; Russia's defence ministry said three children aged 13, 15 and 16 were killed in Krasnodar. Neither account has been independently verified. Ozon shares fell as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange and those of its main shareholder AFK Sistema by almost 13%.

Andy Burnham, on his first overseas trip as UK prime minister, met Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv and chaired his first meeting of the British- and French-led coalition of the willing. Britain agreed to hand over blueprints for UK-made components of the Scalp missile, the French version of the Storm Shadow cruise missile, so Ukraine can build the weapon domestically. Burnham urged the US Congress to 'ratchet up' economic pressure on Russia.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the British missile transfer prevented 'even the slightest progress' towards peace and that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate and destroy any Ukrainian missile production sites. Asked about the charge that Britain was adding fuel to the fire, Burnham replied: 'Who started the fire?'
Ukrainian strikes hit Russia's second-biggest online retailer, extending Kyiv's campaign against Russian commercial and logistics infrastructure.
Britain and Ukraine signed an artificial-intelligence defence partnership covering battlefield technology, extending the industrial cooperation announced during Burnham's visit.

President Vladimir Putin granted the Russian state the right to take control of infrastructure it judges inadequately protected against drone attacks, a response to Ukraine's deepening campaign against Russian economic targets.
Britain and France pledged stronger support as Ukraine marked 35 years of independence, with Burnham saying allies were digging into their own stocks of air defences to help protect Ukrainian skies.

Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev said the Afipsky oil refinery was on fire after a drone attack, and that two people were killed and two injured by falling drone debris at the Afipsky railway station. The account is from Russian regional officials and is not independently verified. The export-focused plant processed about 144,000 barrels a day in 2024, and follows the halt of the Perm refinery after a Ukrainian drone strike on 21 August.

Andrei Fedorov, an adviser to the Kremlin, told BBC Newsnight there might be a 'semi-military' response against UK drone factories by 'unknown sources' over Britain sharing blueprints for Scalp/Storm Shadow missile components. The remark is one adviser's and not a stated Russian government position.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, returning from Kyiv, said he will 'likely' travel to the United States next month with European leaders to lobby President Trump on Ukraine's defence needs, though he said the details were not fully confirmed. It would be his first US trip since taking office in July.

Archbishop Paul Gallagher, the Vatican's foreign minister, met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Moscow — the first in-person Vatican-Russia talks in five years. Gallagher said it was 'urgent and necessary' to end the war, and the two agreed to cooperate on humanitarian matters including children affected by the fighting.

A US Air Force Boeing C-17 Globemaster, tail number 07-7181, flew direct from Riga and landed at Moscow's Vnukovo airport at about 0700 GMT, per Flightradar24 data. It is the first direct flight of a US-registered jet to Russia from Europe since January. The Kremlin said it had no information on the plane; its cargo and passengers could not be verified.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine sees a window for US-led mediation until the end of next summer, and that a one-page set of ideas drafted with US and European officials — a ceasefire as the main point, plus a US-proposed free economic zone in Donbas administered by a third party — will be put to Moscow.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Finnish President Alexander Stubb's approval of Ukrainian long-range strikes inside Russia showed he belonged, alongside Britain's Andy Burnham, to the 'party of war', and accused Western leaders of misleading voters about Russia being strategically defeated.

German investigators found a third drone west of Leipzig/Halle Airport on 14 August, 10 days after the attempted attack, along with about 50g of a substance suspected to be the military explosive hexogen, according to NDR, WDR and the Sueddeutsche Zeitung. Security sources cited in the reports suspect Russian intelligence involvement; Moscow denies it. The prosecutor-general's office did not comment.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (NDR, WDR, Sueddeutsche Zeitung)

timeline.event: Sweden's military said it was seeking to take over a Russian-owned estate close to a Swedish naval base, citing security concerns.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that whoever was behind a drone incident over Germany would 'pay a price'. No party has been formally identified.
Slovak police said they had thwarted a planned arson attack on a drone factory.

German magazine Der Spiegel reported that a man detained over a Berlin gun stash is suspected of being part of a Russian network. The claim comes from the magazine's reporting and has not been confirmed by prosecutors.
Mykhailo Fedorov, recently ousted as defence minister, said Ukraine needs to change how it is fighting to avoid losing the war.

The United States asked Ukraine not to launch air strikes around Moscow, St Petersburg and some northern Russian territories on 24, 25 and 26 August, because a plane carrying a senior US official would be in the area.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow for meetings with Russian officials, CBS News and Axios reported citing unnamed sources — the first known Moscow visit by a US intelligence chief since William Burns met Vladimir Putin in November 2021. The CIA declined to comment; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov neither confirmed nor denied the visit and said Putin had no plans to meet Ratcliffe.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, CNA (CBS News, Axios)

timeline.event: Switzerland will hold a referendum next month on adopting a more restrictive form of neutrality that would bar it from imposing economic sanctions or cooperating with NATO in peacetime.

The BBC reports the CIA director's Moscow trip would be the first known visit by a US spy chief since 2021. The CIA declined to comment and the Kremlin said President Vladimir Putin had no plans to meet him.

The Kremlin said CIA director John Ratcliffe held talks with Russian intelligence counterparts during his Moscow visit, while stating that President Vladimir Putin did not meet him. Neither side described what was discussed.
A Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Tambov region was destroyed by fire after being hit by a drone, the regional governor said. Ukraine did not claim the strike.
The BBC reported that as Ukraine keeps striking Russian oil refineries, Russia has shifted to targeting Ukraine's fuel distribution network, including petrol stations.
Ukraine awarded Elon Musk a high state honour as Kyiv seeks to expand its use of Starlink.
The Kremlin said remarks by ousted Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov showed Kyiv was consumed by infighting. The characterisation is Moscow's; Kyiv has not responded.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that those behind a drone incident over German territory would 'pay a price'. Berlin has not publicly attributed the incident.

Ukraine's military named prominent commanders to lead the defence of the eastern region that Russia is demanding be ceded in any settlement, signalling it intends to hold the ground rather than trade it.

President Donald Trump described CIA director John Ratcliffe's unannounced Moscow trip as a 'semi-routine' mission and said 'something may come out of' it. Neither Washington nor Moscow has said what was discussed.
A US senator said he hoped a 'sledgehammer' package of Russian sanctions would pass Congress next month. The bill has not been scheduled for a vote.
A Pentagon official is to brief NATO allies as a US force-posture review raises questions among European members about the scale of the American commitment to the continent.
France's security chief said he sees new threats following the drone attack at Leipzig. No attribution for that incident has been made public by German or French authorities.

The Wall Street Journal and CBS News reported that CIA director John Ratcliffe used his Moscow visit to warn Russia against attacking NATO members, following US intelligence assessments that Moscow could seek to test the alliance. Neither the White House nor the Kremlin has confirmed the content of the talks.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (WSJ, CBS News)

timeline.event: US officials said the Pentagon's global posture review is preparing options on American troop levels in Europe for Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth by 6 November. No decision has been announced.

Russia launched a large overnight missile and drone attack on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities. Ukraine's air force said the barrage included two Oniks anti-ship cruise missiles, 258 drones and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles, and that nearly 90 per cent of the drones were downed along with one Oniks and seven ballistic missiles. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said ports, grain storage, energy and industrial infrastructure were targeted.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ukrainian Air Force, Ukrainian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: President Volodymyr Zelensky said European allies had made 'important decisions' this week to strengthen Ukrainian air defence and that Ukraine had recently received a small batch of Patriot interceptors, renewing his call for further packages. Kyiv has been short of the US-made interceptors capable of downing ballistic missiles.
Russia said it could strike British military targets in response to Ukraine's use of British-supplied missiles against Russian territory.
A senior aide to President Volodymyr Zelensky said talks between Ukraine and Russia may be possible in September.
Russia's foreign intelligence chief confirmed that he held talks with CIA director John Ratcliffe during the American's unannounced visit to Moscow. Neither government has said what was discussed.

US Defense Under Secretary Elbridge Colby, visiting NATO headquarters in Brussels, pressed European allies to set out how they are taking primary responsibility for the continent's conventional defence, as Washington's six-month review of its force posture in Europe continues.
Slovak prosecutors said suspects had planned an arson attack on Skyeton, a Ukrainian drone manufacturer.
Bulgaria will receive seven minehunter ships from Belgium and the Netherlands to help protect the Black Sea.

theatres.name: US/Israel-Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Six months in, the fight has moved from missiles to money. The sanctions package announced on 24 August targets Iran's oil revenues, banks and trading partners, and a US-led naval blockade is restricting exports, but Tehran still holds power and is betting Washington will not aggressively enforce secondary sanctions on China and India. Mediation is broadening rather than narrowing: Qatar's prime minister flew to Tehran on Thursday while Iran and Oman continue work on a Strait of Hormuz shipping accord. Allied officials privately assess that the strait is still likely mined despite President Trump's claim that it has been cleared.

timeline.event: Yemen's internationally recognised government says the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mocha, killing four civilians. The Houthis have not commented.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the US will step up economic pressure on Iran, as two more ships are reported attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
Abu Dhabi National Oil Company says one of its vessels came under attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz the previous day, according to Emirati state media.
Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian', responding to Trump's threat to declare Hormuz US territory.
Yemen's Mocha port suspends commercial and maritime operations after being hit by more than 25 missiles in Houthi attacks over recent days, the port's management says.
Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots, rejecting Tehran's claim that they have been held since Qatari forces downed two Iranian fighter jets.
Iran accuses Qatar of thwarting the investigation into the fate of the three pilots, according to Iranian state-linked media.
Iran's parliament advances a bill further criminalising interviews given to media the state designates as hostile.

Iran's army chief Amir Hatami announces a bounty of about US$30,000 for the killing or capture of US soldiers, saying the plan followed a 'large number of requests' to take part, according to state news agency IRNA.

The US and Iran pass the 60-day deadline set under June's ceasefire memorandum without agreeing a deal on Iran's nuclear programme. Washington has rescinded oil sanctions waivers and reimposed a naval blockade of Iranian ports; Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed.
President Trump threatens to bomb Oman if it 'gets in the way' of a US deal with Iran on the Strait of Hormuz, according to a report carried by CNA.
Iran says it now considers the three missing pilots to be prisoners held in Qatar, saying they went missing during an operation against Al Udeid Air Base. Doha denies holding them.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says the group attacked a Saudi military ship and four escort vessels off Yemen's Mocha with missiles. Riyadh has not confirmed the claim.
Drones target the office of the Iraqi Kurdistan region's prime minister; no casualties are reported and no group has claimed responsibility.
Iran says two French embassy employees have been barred from returning to the country.

Iran threatens to 'go on the offensive' in the Strait of Hormuz if diplomacy with the United States fails, and says separately it will escalate if Washington does not honour June's memorandum within weeks. The threats are Tehran's own characterisation.
President Trump says Iran will not agree to the deal he believes is needed, and repeats his threat to strike Oman if it obstructs a Hormuz arrangement.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urges Trump to pursue talks with Iran and offers Ankara's support in facilitating them.
Government bond yields jump and oil extends gains after the US-Iran ceasefire deadline passes without an agreement, with US stocks having fallen in the previous session on the same combination.

Iranian fishermen begin venturing back into waters near the Strait of Hormuz despite fears of renewed fighting, an early sign of civilian activity returning to the waterway even as it stays effectively closed to commercial traffic.

Iran's chief negotiator, parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, says the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the United States meets Tehran's conditions under the interim deal signed in June. Washington has not publicly responded to the specific terms.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says it received a report that a vessel transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile, causing engine-room damage and one crew casualty. No party has claimed the strike.
The United Arab Emirates says its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iran, both of which fell into the sea. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the statement as 'baseless'.

President Donald Trump says talks with Iran are neither taking place nor scheduled and asserts the Strait of Hormuz is open. Iran says the waterway will stay closed until Washington meets the terms of June's interim deal.
Trump posts a map showing the Strait of Hormuz as US territory, days after Iran's deputy foreign minister said the strait 'has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian'.
France says it will expel two Iranian diplomats in the coming days over a July incident involving two staff of the French embassy in Tehran.
The US Justice Department unseals charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute over hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies.

The United Arab Emirates halts all trade and financial dealings with Iran, saying its air defences detected two ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory and that Tehran has repeatedly targeted its tankers. Iran's foreign ministry rejects the missile allegation as baseless.
Iran warns Gulf countries against assisting the United States militarily, after the UAE's decision to cut trade ties.

The Straits Times reports that the UAE's financial embargo puts the long-standing Abu Dhabi-Tehran rivalry back in the spotlight, with the UAE having been one of Iran's largest trade and re-export partners.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz slows further as uncertainty over the waterway's status persists.

The US Justice Department's charges against 17 people it links to Iran's Mabna Institute are reported in full, covering hacking of US universities, companies and government agencies. The defendants are not in US custody.
Iran says its ambassador has met four Iranian nationals detained in Kuwait. Kuwaiti authorities have not commented publicly.
An Iranian academic detained in the United States over an alleged link to the 1979 hostage crisis writes about conditions in US detention, in an account published by the BBC.

President Donald Trump says on Truth Social that the United States is launching 'the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country' against Iran, saying Tehran failed to take the chance to make a deal. No sanctions list has been published.

Trump warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Iran 'any type of lifeline' will face 'tremendous economic consequences'. The administration has not named which states it means.

The US warns that Siemens programmable logic controllers can be exploited, amid concern that Iranian-linked actors are breaching water treatment plants. CISA has issued advisories; no confirmed compromise of a US utility has been announced.

Analysts tell Al Jazeera that maintenance problems aboard the carrier USS Abraham Lincoln illustrate the limits of sustaining US naval presence through a prolonged Iran conflict. The Navy has not commented on the assessment.

Trump says he will impose tougher economic measures on Iran and warns that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities give Tehran 'any type of lifeline' will face consequences. No sanctions list or named target country has been published.

Iranian officials publicly deride Trump's threat of 'economic warfare'. Separately, Iran's military says it is prepared to conduct offensive strikes as diplomacy with Washington stalls; the statement is Tehran's and has not been independently corroborated.

The Straits Times reports that Iran's practical control over traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is slipping, while the United States is far from having secured the waterway - leaving both sides short of their stated aims.
The US Justice Department charges 17 Iranian nationals linked to the Mabna Institute over an alleged US$3.4 billion theft of academic and corporate data. The defendants are not in US custody.

US agencies including the NSA, CISA, the FBI, the Department of Energy and the EPA warn that attackers are using AI-generated tooling against Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, with water treatment operators among the concerns.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the coming sanctions will be the toughest in history, will 'squash' Iran's economy and that Washington intends to 'collapse this regime', suggesting the move lessens the need for new major military operations. No details of the measures have been released.
The BBC reports that Iran has for years proved adept at working around punishing sanctions, raising doubts about how much the threatened measures would bite.
The US Treasury issues fresh sanctions on Hezbollah, including re-designating it under a terrorism authority, in a move framed around the group's links to the Iranian government.
A new US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been on station for an extended deployment.
Yemen's Houthis say they targeted a Saudi airport and a Saudi Aramco facility. Saudi authorities have not confirmed any damage and the claim is not independently verified.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war: 'It is better that we bring the war to an end now as we are in a position of power and dignity.' It is the clearest signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership that Tehran wants an exit, and follows its foreign ministry accusing Washington of 'economic terrorism'.

The chief of staff of Iran's armed forces, Major-General Ali Abdollahi, says Tehran will answer new US threats with 'crushing, punishing and devastating responses' across land, sea, air, air defence and cyberspace, according to Iranian media. Parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says Washington appears to have concluded it cannot prevail militarily.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says details of the threatened sanctions package will be published on Aug 24, after saying the measures will be the toughest in history and are intended to collapse the Iranian government.
China says US 'sanctions and pressure' will not resolve the conflict and urges a political solution, rebuffing Washington's request that Beijing help isolate Iran's economy.
A teenager pleads guilty in London over an arson attack on the offices of the Persian-language broadcaster Iran International.

NATO's supreme allied commander, US Air Force General Alexus Grynkewich, hosted a chiefs-of-defence videoconference on Aug 19 to help interested allies coordinate possible contributions to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. His spokesperson stresses it is not a NATO mission; France and Britain have been assembling a coalition of about a dozen countries to guarantee safe passage, which would ultimately need Iranian acquiescence.

President Masoud Pezeshkian says it is time to end the war 'while we are in a position of power and dignity' - the clearest exit signal yet from Iran's civilian leadership, delivered as Washington prepares to publish its sanctions package on Aug 24.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei calls the imminent US sanctions package an 'assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty over every independent member state of the United Nations' with 'no foundation in international law'. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to detail the measures at a press conference at 2pm EDT on Monday and is pressing Beijing to cooperate; China, which buys more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil on 2025 Kpler data, has urged diplomacy instead. The two sides are neither exchanging fire nor holding talks.

Ship-tracking data shows only four commodity ships transited the Strait of Hormuz on Aug 20, none of them large crude or LNG carriers, with thousands of seafarers stranded on hundreds of vessels. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the US military helped move a seven-day average of 8 million barrels a day through the strait, against more than 20 million a day before the war.

Iran grants permission for a number of Iraqi oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, state news agency IRNA reports. Iraqi President Nizar Amedi says passage has been facilitated in recent days but calls the issue complicated. Traffic remains far below pre-war levels and ships continue to face attacks.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (IRNA, Iraqi President Nizar Amedi)

timeline.event: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent schedules a 2pm EDT Monday press conference to unveil the sanctions package, having promised 'the toughest sanctions in history' and urged Beijing to cooperate. China buys more than 80% of Iran's shipped oil, according to 2025 data from analytics firm Kpler, and has urged diplomacy.
Two US tanker aircraft leave Bulgaria's Bezmer air base, the Bulgarian defence minister says, nearly a month after their deployment angered Tehran.
An Iranian official urges Qatar to move detained pilots from a vessel to a hospital on land.

Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei denounces the US plan to announce new sanctions, calling it an 'assertion of extraterritorial sovereignty' over other states. CNA notes that after nearly six months since the US and Israel began strikes on Feb 28, the sides are not firing at each other but show no sign of peace talks, and that oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz are at a virtual standstill.

Mohsen Rezai, head of Iran's supreme national security council, warns on state television that any country joining the US 'economic war' will be 'considered an enemy'. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to detail the package on Monday; China, which buys more than 80% of Iran's shipped oil according to 2025 Kpler data, has urged diplomacy.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Iranian state television)

timeline.event: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi dismisses the threatened US sanctions as 'repetitive scenarios' and a sign of desperation, saying they will fail to defeat Tehran. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to detail the package at a 2pm EDT press conference on Monday, having promised 'the toughest sanctions in history'.

Iran executes a man it accused of aiding the United States and Israel during anti-government protests. The charges and the trial process are Iranian state accounts and have not been independently verified.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent writes in the Financial Times that 'at dawn begins an economic D-Day - the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary', trailing sanctions aimed at Iran's trading partners.

Iran says it has discovered a gas field holding more than 200 billion cubic metres, after the war damaged its energy sector. The claim comes from Iranian officials and has not been independently verified.

Iran vows to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf 'if the economic war continues', and warns that any country supporting the US sanctions will be treated as taking a hostile act. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is already near a standstill.

Oil prices fall as traders weigh the scale of the threatened US sanctions against the prospect of Iranian retaliation. Bessent is due to hold a press conference at 1pm EDT on 24 Aug (1am on 25 Aug Singapore time).

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Washington will sever all economic ties with Iran in 'an economic D-Day', calling it 'the single greatest financial offensive ever' and claiming the war is 'entering its endgame'. Writing in the Financial Times, he says any nation partnering with Iran financially will also be isolated, but gives no detail on the measures; he is due to set them out at a press conference at 1pm US Eastern time (1am Singapore time on 25 August).

Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi mocks the threat as an admission of American defeat, arguing on X that Washington cannot simultaneously claim Iran's military and nuclear capabilities were destroyed and that the largest financial offensive in history is still needed.

Iran's newly created Persian Gulf Strait Authority warns that vessels breaching its Strait of Hormuz transit arrangements face restrictions including fines, detention or confiscation, and says ships doing ship-to-ship transfers with non-compliant vessels will themselves be added to a restricted list.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Persian Gulf Strait Authority)

timeline.event: Pakistan's army chief flies to Tehran on a mediating mission as the US prepares the sanctions package. Pakistan previously brokered a de-escalation after Trump's April ultimatum.
South Korea says the United States has cancelled a joint marine exercise because of the Iran war, the latest sign of US forces being redirected towards the Gulf.
Iran says it has found a new gas field, which officials present as a cushion after the war damaged its energy sector.

Oil transits through the Strait of Hormuz ran at five million barrels per day, provisional data from shiptracker Vortexa showed, against more than 20 million per day before the war — about one in every five barrels consumed worldwide.

At a Washington press conference on Monday branded 'Operation Economic Outcast', US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced sanctions determinations against five Iranian sectors — digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping — plus measures against almost 60 entities, individuals and vessels. He called it 'the single greatest financial offensive ever' and said America was 'no longer managing the Iranian threat, we are ending it'.

Iran's economy minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran has a two-year plan to counter the sanctions and that they would end in another defeat for Washington. Iran repeated that it would shut down all oil exports from the region if the war continues.

Analysts noted the package stopped short of the harshest options the White House had threatened. Oil prices fell as traders read the announcement as more moderate than the 'economic D-Day' language suggested.
Pakistan's army chief met Iran's president in Tehran, continuing Islamabad's mediation effort as the sanctions package landed.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Iran had 'tried to kill' one of his sons. The claim has not been independently verified and Iran has not commented publicly on it.

Iran's economy minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran was 'fully prepared' for the new sanctions and predicted 'another defeat' for Washington, telling state television that neither China nor Russia had accepted the measures and that other countries would resist them. The UAE, one of Iran's largest trading partners alongside China and Turkey, announced last week it was halting all trade and financial transactions with Tehran.

The International Maritime Organization confirmed 68 maritime incidents in the Gulf and neighbouring waters over the six months of the war, in which at least 20 workers were killed, 35 wounded and one is missing, mostly on tankers. The rate slowed to no casualties during the peace talks and returned to roughly one incident every 2.8 days after they collapsed.

Pakistan's interior minister said talks in Tehran had made 'significant progress', with Pakistan's military saying the meetings between army chief Asim Munir and the Iranian leadership covered preventing further escalation, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and expediting an end to the conflict. The characterisation is Islamabad's; Tehran has not issued a matching statement and no terms have been published.

The US Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control named Singapore-based Wellbred Capital, with trading arms in the UAE and Switzerland, among close to 60 companies, individuals and vessels designated over Iran links, citing ties to Iranian oil shipping figure Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.

Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said Beijing's cooperation with Iran is conducted within the framework of international law and 'should not be interfered with or disrupted', and that China would take 'all necessary measures' to safeguard its rights and interests after Washington widened sanctions.

The New York Times reported, citing an internal State Department document, that Washington is preparing to return Foreign Service officers to Middle East embassies evacuated before and during the war, including in Israel, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan, Oman, Iraq and Kuwait, possibly from this week. The report is not independently verified; the department said it 'continuously reviews' its security posture.
Long queues formed at petrol stations in Tehran after Washington announced fresh sanctions, a day after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent set out plans for the 'economic asphyxiation' of Iran.
Iran and Oman said they had discussed opening a temporary corridor through the Strait of Hormuz along with mine-clearing work. No timetable or mechanism was announced.

President Donald Trump said on Truth Social that all mines had been detonated or removed from international waters in the Strait of Hormuz, that the US Space Force was watching 'every square inch', and that Iran had been told any vessel placing new mines would be destroyed. Iran has not confirmed the account.
The US Secret Service said it was aware of an Iranian video threat against Barron Trump, the president's son. The service did not describe the threat as credible.
China's foreign ministry called the widened US sanctions on Iran and its trading partners 'illegal', with spokesperson Lin Jian saying Beijing's cooperation with Tehran should not be disrupted.
Oil prices fell as traders weighed the threat of wider US sanctions on Iran and its trading partners, suggesting markets are not pricing an immediate supply shock.

Iran and Oman said they had discussed opening a temporary corridor through the Strait of Hormuz together with mine-clearing work, as the impasse with Washington drags on. Neither government gave a timeline and the account has not been independently verified.
Ship-tracking data showed Gulf traffic through the Strait of Hormuz still running below its 10-day average, despite President Donald Trump's statement that the waterway had been cleared of mines.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said no diplomatic deal was possible with Iran, calling its leadership 'savages'. Tehran has not responded to the remark.
Gulf air hubs are absorbing a wartime downturn in traffic, with carriers and airports reporting reduced volumes through the conflict.
A senior Iranian source said Iran and Oman are still working on an accord covering shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. No timetable or mechanism has been given by either government.
Qatar's prime minister will travel to Tehran to pursue mediation efforts, adding a second Gulf channel alongside Oman's.

Allied officials privately assess that the Strait of Hormuz is still likely mined, saying demining has not cleared all of the estimated 80 to 150 mines laid by Iran and that sea currents have moved many of them from their original positions. The assessment challenges President Donald Trump's repeated statement that the strait is clear; US Central Command declined to comment. Iran has opposed foreign mine-clearing operations in the strait.
Qatar's prime minister travelled to Tehran to pursue mediation efforts, opening a second Gulf channel alongside Oman's talks with Iran.

Six months after US and Israeli forces attacked Iran on 28 February, The Straits Times assessed the war as a costly stalemate: Washington's sanctions package announced on 24 August shifts the fight from missiles to Iran's oil revenues, banks and trading partners, while a US-led naval blockade restricts its exports. Tehran is betting that Washington will not aggressively enforce secondary sanctions on China and India.
A Greek-operated air defence system shot down drones over Saudi Arabia.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: The quietest of the three theatres this cycle. There was no significant military development in the last 24 hours; the freshest substantive entries are from 26 August, when Israel's seizure of UNRWA's Qalandia training college in East Jerusalem drew international condemnation and Lebanon accused Israel of setting fire to forest and farmland in the south. Israel has not commented on the Lebanese accusation. Gaza casualty accounts in this timeline come from Gazan medical sources and have not been independently verified.

timeline.event: Palestinians are told to leave homes in the West Bank village of Qusra that Israeli settlers had besieged.
